paper.title_en: Adaptive noise-mitigated distributed variational quantum sensing with federated learning
paper.abstract_en: Quantum sensor networks (QSNs) enable collaborative parameter estimation across distributed quantum sensors, improving sensing precision, spatial coverage, and robustness over standalone systems. However, practical QSNs are intrinsically heterogeneous and time-varying, as sensor nodes may experience different decoherence rates, idle times, hardware noise, measurement shot budgets, and communication constraints. Existing variational quantum sensing methods are often unsuitable for large-scale networked sensing because they typically rely on centralized optimization or assume uniform device conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a heterogeneity-aware noise-mitigated federated circuit learning (FCL) framework for distributed variational quantum sensing. Each sensor locally optimizes a parameterized sensing circuit using a Fisher-information-based Cramér-Rao bound objective, while a central server periodically aggregates circuit parameters to extract shared sensing knowledge without collecting raw quantum measurement outcomes. Unlike standard federated averaging, which enforces a single global circuit across all sensors, the proposed personalized FCL decomposes circuit parameters into shared global parameters and sensor-specific personalization vectors. This design enables local adaptation to heterogeneous noise, resource constraints, and representation drift. To mitigate pre-encoding decoherence in the prepared probe state, we further employ adaptive dynamical decoupling (DD), where each sensor selects a DD sequence according to its idle duration, local dephasing rate, and pulse-control overhead. The DD policy is formulated as a multiarmed bandit problem to balance sensing accuracy, timing cost, and pulse-control error under time-varying conditions. We also provide convergence analysis under DD-related gradient noise, device heterogeneity, and finite-shot estimation noise. Demonstrations on variational Ramsey spectroscopy simulations show that the proposed framework improves estimation precision over standalone optimization, homogeneous FCL, heterogeneous federated averaging, and quantum sensing baselines, while maintaining communication-efficient parameter exchange.
